points.quote: Examiners across all programmes of study (including Undergraduate, Postgraduate Taught, and Postgraduate Research) are not permitted to upload, copy, or share student work with Generative AI (GenAI) tools and Large Language Models (LLMs).
points.gist: Examiners may not upload, copy or share student work with GenAI tools or LLMs.

points.quote: Examiners may not use tools, such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google Bard, or Microsoft Copilot, to analyse work submitted by students and provide written feedback.
points.gist: Examiners may not use tools such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Bard or Copilot to analyse student work and give written feedback.

points.quote: Where preferred, however, examiners may use these tools to support their own writing in the process of documenting feedback (e.g., consolidating personal notes and rephrasing comments).
points.gist: Examiners may use these tools to support their own writing when documenting feedback, such as consolidating notes and rephrasing comments.

points.quote: “A student using any unacknowledged content generated by artificial intelligence within a summative assessment as though it is their own work constitutes academic misconduct, unless explicitly stated otherwise in the assessment brief.”
points.gist: Unacknowledged AI-generated content in a summative assessment presented as your own is academic misconduct, unless the assessment brief says otherwise.

points.quote: Not relying on AI detection software as it is not proven to be accurate or reliable and provides no evidence to support investigations into the use of GenAI.
points.gist: Staff are recommended not to rely on AI detection software, which is not proven accurate or reliable and gives no investigative evidence.

points.quote: Designing assessments that require information or skills that is more difficult for GenAI tools to replicate such as personal reflection.
points.gist: Staff are recommended to design assessments needing skills harder for GenAI to replicate, such as personal reflection.

points.quote: Consider how students, where permitted to use GenAI, should declare their use and describe how it was used within their work.
points.gist: Staff should consider how students, where permitted, should declare and describe their GenAI use.

points.quote: There are a wide variety of use-cases and possible variations across the University so students should always review local guidance from their department or faculty as well as information in the assignment itself.
points.gist: Students should always review local department or faculty guidance and the assignment itself.

points.quote: Provide clear guidance and rationale for permitting or prohibiting use of GenAI in assessments to support student understanding and compliance
points.gist: Staff should give clear guidance and rationale for permitting or prohibiting GenAI use in assessments.
